texts: good. a fireable rule: the heir, the inheriting and the Keeper's lantern-station are all minted per retiring Keeper, the inheriting is tied to the retirement, and 'that Keeper's' binds back to the condition.
good. the same clean shape as the retirement variant — the death is the trigger, the heir and the station are minted per Keeper, and the inheriting is tied to the death.

mixed: every atom is right, but 'A Keeper's family' with an ordinary verb reads as one particular family on one occasion, so your world rule is recorded as a single situation rather than a generalization about Keepers — a singular 'a' never becomes a rule; only a bare plural, an explicit quantifier, or a when/whenever clause does. Rewrite as: 'When a Keeper inherits a station, that Keeper's family keeps it.'
good. becomes a fireable rule obliging the Council to approve every station transfer, with 'any' recorded as the quantifier word and the transfer compound decomposed.
